text(await tools.apply_patch("*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: /Users/jamie/development/exposed-funder-resolution-20261007/.design/funder-resolution/why-investigation.md
+# Funder resolution: historical constraints
+
+## Question and anchor
+
+Why does the current cleaner preserve separate observations and emit matching features without resolving identities, and what can the older importer teach the proposed resolution CLI?
+
+Baseline: `main` at `9e4de95`. Anchors: `docs/declaration-cleaning.md:41`, `exposed/src/lib/domain/models/declaration_cleaning.rs:90`, `funder_name.rs:1`, and `exposed/src/lib/inbound/cli.rs:92`. The Python `ingest/src/exposed/declaration_importer.py` is now a compatibility entry point; its attribution policy lives in `core/declarations.py` and persistence in `adapters/declaration_postgres.py`.
+
+## What we found
+
+- **Direct rationale:** PR #22 states that raw capture combines declaration, funding and funder evidence, and introduces an offline cleaning step for separate funding entries and observations “with feature columns for later entity resolution.” Its tradeoff says: “Equal name features can support later matching without prematurely merging people or organisations.” This explicitly answers why equality does not merge observations. Author: `johnnylarner`, 7 October 2026. [PR #22](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/pull/22).
+- **Direct scope:** The same PR says: “Entity resolution, parent attribution and database loading remain separate stages.” This is a boundary of that cleaning change, not a permanent prohibition on adding resolution. [PR #22](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/pull/22).
+- **Direct documented policy:** The cleaner's reference defines roles and scopes, retains source pointers, assigns donor metadata only to donor observations, and says matching names remain distinct. Features are candidates, never entity IDs. Missing and withheld names carry no primary matching features. `docs/declaration-cleaning.md:43–66,89–91`.
+- **Direct documented legacy limitation:** The Python importer's shared normalized name is “a storage key, not verified identity matching.” Its database model reuses a UUID for repeated standardized names, updates explicit metadata with the last imported value, and retains omitted metadata. `ingest/README.md:74–78,120–137`; `adapters/declaration_postgres.py:86–108`. These document behavior, not a reason that exact-name identity is safe.
+- **Direct historical design context:** The old specification says financial declarations include several funders, in-kind benefits and parent-held payer information. It chose a simple model for useful financial fields, selecting the ultimate payer rather than retaining alternative payer identities. Source examples informed that model; an ultimate-payer payment and a parent-payer payment are explicitly cited as evidence for preserving parent relationships. Historical `docs/specs/declaration-ingestion.md` at `4d71106:17–29,239–244` (the file is absent on current main).
+- **Supported policy continuity, not proof of identity:** Tests cover ultimate-payer preference, preserving donor-group metadata, refusing donor metadata for a different ultimate payer, and sharing names without collapsing payments. This converges with the documentation on a single attributed payer plus exact-name storage design. `ingest/tests/test_funder_identification.py:95–148`, `test_funder_storage.py:19–40`, `core/declarations.py:47–64`.
+- **Direct history:** #9 restored name normalization from `95ab25b`; its body gives no explanation beyond recovery. #8 adds shared funder identities but has an empty PR body. #17 has no descriptive body and its only inline review says “We don't need this” on README.md; this is about that documentation, not an entity-resolution policy. [PR #9](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/pull/9), [PR #8](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/pull/8), [PR #17 review](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/pull/17#discussion_r4173930815).
+
+## Reasonable inference
+
+- **Inferred:** Separate observations appear to make later decisions auditable and revisable: source IDs and pointers survive, while multiple interpretations of names are available in parallel. #22 explicitly postpones merges; the cleaner reference supplies the traceability machinery. Reversibility as an author motivation is not separately stated.
+- **Inferred:** Legacy ultimate-payer preference appears aimed at reporting who ultimately funded a payment in a compact display model. The historical problem statement, selected-name design and source examples support that reading. It does not justify discarding donor or intermediary evidence in a new resolution stage.
+- **Inferred:** Exact-name sharing was likely a pragmatic storage simplification. The docs explicitly disclaim verified matching and tests exercise UUID reuse. No source inspected explains why exact standardized name was preferred over company numbers or probabilistic resolution.
+
+## Unknowns and competing explanations
+
+We found no documented accuracy target, fuzzy threshold, approved clustering rule, adjudication workflow, external registry policy or collision-handling rationale. Neither #8 nor #9 records why its precise normalization rules were chosen. Simplicity and historical implementation convenience both fit exact-name sharing; the record does not distinguish them. #22 records reported verification counts but supplies no measured entity-resolution precision or recall.
+
+The legacy name-sharing contract differs from the current observation contract. This is a change of stage and output meaning, not evidence that current observations should inherit legacy UUID equality or last-write-wins metadata.
+
+## Sources consulted and coverage
+
+- **Source control:** Path histories for cleaner models/docs and legacy importer; commit messages/details for `9e4de95`, `6d41414`, `46b792a`, `5f4c05a`, `34a4de8`, `4d71106`, `eef6697`; historical spec at `4d71106`; current docs, domain comments, CLI and named tests. Queries: `git log --oneline -- <paths>`, `git show -s --format=fuller <commits>`, `git show <commit>:<path>`, `rg 'funder|identify|match|ultimate|preferred|exact'`. Read PR bodies/reviews #22/#17 and inline comments through `gh`; followed legacy history to #8/#9. No implementation executed.
+- **Issue tracker:** Skipped under the explicit teach investigation scope (git, repository docs/tests and relevant PRs). #16 appears in #17's commit message but was not opened.
+- **Long-form documents:** Repository documentation above searched. External document connectors skipped under the explicit narrowed scope; no unrelated personal documents queried.
+- **Real-time team chat:** Skipped under the explicit narrowed scope.
+- **Infrastructure observability:** Skipped under the explicit narrowed scope.
+- **Error/exception tracking:** Skipped under the explicit narrowed scope.
+- **Product analytics warehouse:** Skipped under the explicit narrowed scope; no database access or queries.
+
+## Planning constraints
+
+- **Preserve:** Raw evidence, observation identities, role/scope/source pointers, repeated funding occurrences and absent/withheld status. Keep donor metadata attached to its source role. These are documented cleaner contracts, not future entity decisions.
+- **Change:** Add an explicit resolution stage whose results link observations to proposed or accepted entities. Treat cleaner features as evidence inputs. The separate-stage boundary in #22 permits this extension without changing what cleaner IDs mean.
+- **Avoid:** Reusing legacy normalized-name uniqueness as proof of real identity; erasing source observations when names match; attributing donor company numbers to other roles; treating all confidential placeholders as one person; interpreting controller text or conjunctions as automatic aliases/splits. `docs/declaration-cleaning.md:57–66,89–111` and legacy metadata tests provide the evidence for these constraints.
+- **Risk:** False merges can spread transitively through weaker aliases, initials or common names; exact company-number conflicts and conflicting donor kinds need an explicit policy; resolution must distinguish identifying an entity from selecting which role funded a payment. These are design risks inferred from the available features and role distinctions, not recorded production incidents.
+
+## Confidence summary
+
+The cleaner's separation and deferred identity decisions have direct PR evidence. Legacy behavior and display-oriented constraints are documented, but its exact matching policy's motivation and any safe automatic-resolution rules remain uncertain. Teaching should state those gaps before implementation.
*** End Patch"));
